messages.subject: micro_global vs micro_ncep
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am playing with the functions micro_ncep and micro_global to obtain microclimates for various locations in South Africa. I compared the results for the same location yearly mean and what I am getting is quite different (I am attaching an example of what I obtained for solar irradiance at 0% shade). From my understanding both are based on the NicheMapR microclimate model and the difference lays in the daily weather database used. So how should I choose between them?
So far the only thing I struggled with is that micro_ncep doesn't allow you to set the soil type (e.g. my animals are standing on rocks even if the substrate around is sand. So I guess soilgrid would count the substrate as "sand" but that wouldn't be relevant in my case) making me leaning towards micro_global.
What are your opinions?

Fede

messages.subject: Re: micro_global vs micro_ncep
messages.body_plain:
Hi there Fede,

Are you using the most recent version of NicheMapR? There were some issues with an earlier version of microclima in the way it feed into the micro_ncep function as well as a few other things that got straightened out. Note that the micro_ncep function uses the NCEP solar radiation (6-hourly interpolated to hourly) whereas the micro_global computes it from first principles and the given cloud cover.

More generally, the micro_global function is using a monthly long-term average climatology (1960-1990) while the micro_ncep allows you to use historical forcing data. Which is the more suitable dataset depends very much on what question you're trying to answer.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: NicheMapR v2.0.0 now released
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I've released a new version of NicheMapR with a finalised version of the ectotherm/DEB modelling functions and a beta version of the endotherm model. There is also now a website with lots of resources about NicheMapR at http://mrke.github.io/

A paper will come out shortly in Ecography on the ectotherm and DEB models - I'll post something here when it does.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject_clean: Funny histogram of body temperatures coming out of ecto
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael,

When running micro and ecto for different locations at North America, I keep getting a histogram of body temperatures(tc) from ecto$environ that seem a bit unexpected to me:

values over CTmax are more frequent than values right over VTmax. I wonder how could this happen even for the case when I allow the lizard to find a reasonably deep burrow under the shade.  My first thought was that I was leaving any parameter in an unreasonable level, but after tweaking around, I could not find which it could be. Maybe the animal is bouncing back to the surface and frying there, when it reaches its VTMAx in the burrow, but how reasonable that can be for so deep burrows (2m deep)? Also, for such a hot place, the most frequent body temperatures go pretty under the preferred ones, might these be body temperatures during the night?

Here is my code and and the resultant histogram of body temperatures. Thank you very much for your time and for this splendid tool!
lon= -109.3458
lat= 28.4375
        micro=  micro_global(loc = c(lon,lat),
                    timeinterval=timeinterval,
                    nyears=nyears,
                    Usrhyt=0.004 ,
                    soiltype=2,
                    REFL= 0.1,
                    slope= 0,
                    aspect= 30,
                    DEP=c(0,2,5,10,15,30,60,90,100,120),
                    minshade= 10,
                    maxshade= 100,
                    RUF = 0.004,
                    PCTWET = 100,
                    CMH2O = 1,
                    runmoist=1
)

  Ww_g= 3 #
  ,shape= 3#
  ,T_F_max =42#
  ,T_pref= 35#
  ,T_B_min=20
  ,T_RB_min=20
  ,CT_max=45#
  ,CT_min=0
  ,climb=1
  ,shade_seek=1
  ,burrow  = 1
  ,shdburrow = 1
  ,mindepth    = 1 #
  ,maxdepth    = 7 #
  ,M_1    = 2.454#
  ,M_2    = 0.800#
  ,M_3    = 0.038#
  ,CT_kill = 0
  )

t=as.data.frame(ecto$environ[,c(1:5)])
hist(t$TC)

messages.subject: Re: Funny histogram of body temperatures coming out of ecto
messages.subject_clean: Funny histogram of body temperatures coming out of ecto
messages.body_plain:
Dear Agus,

Glad you're enjoying playing with the models!

I can see where the problem is - you have a value of 2.454 for the parameter M_1, which is one of the three coefficients for the response of metabolic rate to temperature and body mass. This results in a metabolic rate almost 200 times what it would be for a lizard :). That's why they are getting so hot, especially as body temperature rises. Note also that you should not have a value for the Usrhyt parameter (local height you're simulating with the microclimate model) that is lower than the roughness height parameter RUF, because otherwise the microclimate model won't run. The parameter settings you have posted above for the microclimate model returns an error.

In general, when you see something odd happening, it can help to systematically delete your parameter specifications (and thereby let them be the default value), to help figure out what is causing the issue.

All the best,
Mike
